newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb hits Corsica after "truce" expires.
newsitem.headline: Bomb hits Corsica after "truce" expires.

text.p: A bomb exploded in Corsica on Monday, the first blast on the Mediterranean island since a little-respected truce by separatist guerrillas formally expired at the weekend.
The explosion in the centre of Ajaccio at 2.40 a.m. (0040 GMT) damaged a building a few metres (yards) from police headquarters and government offices. No one was hurt.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the blast, the first since a 10-month truce by the hardline Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC)-Historic Wing, already shattered by dozens of blasts, expired on Saturday.

A bomb exploded outside a post office in the town of Folelli on Friday. Last weekend, bombers made a rare attack on the mainland with a blast at city hall in Bordeaux, where conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe is mayor.
Paris has since sent hundreds of police reinforcements to the island after Juppe pledged to crack down on guerrillas pushing for more autonomy from the mainland.

Pierre Pasquini, a Corsican mayor and junior minister for veterans' affairs, said one possibility to help defuse the 22-year Corsican struggle would be to dissolve the local territorial assembly and hold new elections.

A vote would test support for separatists, shown by opinion polls to represent only a minority of the island's 250,000 inhabitants, he said in an interview with Radio Monte Carlo. An election "is a possibility, that's all," he said.
